title: Local Carbon Policy
venue: Advances in Economics and Econometrics, Twelfth World Congress
abstract: We study local carbon policy to address the consequences of climate change. Standard analysis suggests that the social cost of carbon determines optimal carbon policy. We start by using the spatial integrated assessment model in Cruz and Rossi-Hansberg (2021) to measure the local social monetary cost of CO2 emissions: the Local Social Cost of Carbon (LSCC). Although the largest welfare costs from global warming are concentrated in the warmest parts of the developing world, adjusting for the local marginal utility of income implies that the LSCC peaks in warm and high-income regions like the southern parts of the U.S. and Europe, as well as Australia. We then proceed to study the effect of the actual carbon reduction pledges in the Paris Agreement and the progress they can make in implementing the expressed goal of keeping global temperature increases below 2°C. We find that although the distribution of pledges is roughly in line with the LSCC, their magnitude is largely insufficient to achieve its goals. The required carbon taxes necessary to keep temperatures below 2°C over the current century are an order of magnitude higher and involve large implicit inter-temporal transfers. Increasing the elasticity of substitution across energy sources is important to reduce the carbon taxes necessary to achieve warming goals.
abstract_zh: 我们研究地方碳政策，以应对气候变化的后果。标准分析表明，碳的社会成本决定最优碳政策。我们首先利用Cruz和Rossi-Hansberg（2021）的空间综合评估模型，测算CO2排放的地方社会货币成本，即地方碳的社会成本（LSCC）。尽管全球变暖带来的最大福利损失集中在发展中国家最炎热的地区，但在对当地边际收入效用进行调整后，LSCC在美国南部、欧洲南部以及澳大利亚等温暖且高收入地区达到峰值。随后，我们研究了《巴黎协定》中实际碳减排承诺的效果，以及这些承诺在实现将全球气温升幅控制在2°C以内这一既定目标方面所取得的进展。我们发现，尽管承诺的分布与LSCC大体一致，但其规模在很大程度上不足以实现相关目标。若要在本世纪内将气温控制在2°C以内，所需的碳税要高出一个数量级，并涉及大规模的隐性跨期转移。提高能源来源之间的替代弹性，对于降低实现增温目标所需的碳税至关重要。

title: Closing the Border: The Impact of U.S. Migration and Trade Policy
Evaluating the Spatial Consequences of a Climate Tipping Point
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that plays a key role in regulating global climate, including moderating temperatures in Europe and the North Atlantic. Its potential collapse due to global warming is widely considered one of the more likely climate tipping points. This paper examines the economic implications of such a collapse using a dynamic spatially integrated assessment model (S-IAM) of the world economy. Scandinavia and parts of Russia are predicted to experience significant losses in GDP and welfare, while southern Europe, northern Africa, and Brazil benefit from slightly colder temperatures. S-IAMs generally predict that global warming is especially harmful to low-income regions, but an AMOC collapse could mitigate some of these negative impacts in parts of the developing world while instead harming some of the more advanced economies. This lowers spatial inequality, but global welfare drops by 1.9% by 2200 under an intermediate-emissions scenario. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 大西洋经向翻转环流（AMOC）是一套洋流系统，在调节全球气候方面发挥着关键作用，包括缓和欧洲和北大西洋的气温。全球变暖可能导致其崩溃，这被广泛认为是较有可能出现的气候临界点之一。本文利用一个动态空间综合评估模型（S-IAM）考察了此类崩溃的经济影响。模型预测，斯堪的纳维亚和俄罗斯部分地区将遭受显著的GDP与福利损失，而南欧、北非和巴西则因气温略微降低而受益。S-IAM通常预测，全球变暖对低收入地区尤为有害，但AMOC崩溃可能在一定程度上减轻发展中国家部分地区的负面影响，同时却会损害一些较为发达的经济体。这降低了空间不平等，但在中等排放情景下，到2200年全球福利将下降1.9%。NBER工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可以在 www.nber.org 免费下载本文。
